Unlimited Liability.description: Contract imposes no cap on damages, exposing the signing party to unlimited financial liability.
Unlimited Liability.plain_language: You could owe unlimited money if something goes wrong.
Unlimited Liability.recommendation: Negotiate a liability cap — typically 1x or 2x the contract value.

IP Ownership Assigned.description: Intellectual property created during the engagement is assigned to the other party.
IP Ownership Assigned.plain_language: Anything you build or create under this contract belongs to them, not you.
IP Ownership Assigned.recommendation: Retain ownership of pre-existing IP. Negotiate joint ownership or license-back for work product.

Non-Compete.description: Restricts the signing party from working with competitors or in related industries.
Non-Compete.plain_language: You may be blocked from working with other companies in your sector.
Non-Compete.recommendation: Limit scope (geography, duration, industry). Broad non-competes are often unenforceable in India.

Auto-Renewal.description: Contract renews automatically without explicit action, potentially locking in unfavorable terms.
Auto-Renewal.plain_language: This contract renews itself — you could be locked in for another year without realizing it.
Auto-Renewal.recommendation: Add a notice period (30–60 days) for non-renewal and ensure opt-out rights.

Termination for Convenience.description: One or both parties can terminate without cause. Direction determines who benefits.
Termination for Convenience.plain_language: The contract can be ended without reason — check whether this applies to them, you, or both.
Termination for Convenience.recommendation: Ensure termination for convenience is mutual, with adequate notice period (30–90 days).

Indemnification.description: One party must compensate the other for losses, damages, or legal costs.
Indemnification.plain_language: You may have to pay their legal fees and losses if something goes wrong — even for things outside your control.
Indemnification.recommendation: Ensure indemnification is mutual and limited to direct damages caused by your negligence.

Price Restrictions.description: Restricts the signing party from changing pricing, discounting, or offering different terms.
Price Restrictions.plain_language: Your pricing flexibility may be restricted by this agreement.
Price Restrictions.recommendation: Negotiate carve-outs for promotional pricing and minimum advertised price policies.

Liquidated Damages.description: Pre-specified penalty amounts triggered by defined breaches.
Liquidated Damages.plain_language: If you breach certain terms, you automatically owe a fixed penalty amount.
Liquidated Damages.recommendation: Ensure penalty amounts are reasonable and proportionate to actual potential harm.

Governing Law.description: Specifies which jurisdiction's laws govern the contract.
Governing Law.plain_language: Disputes will be resolved under the laws of a specific state or country.
Governing Law.recommendation: For Indian startups, prefer Indian governing law (Maharashtra or Karnataka courts are common).

Audit Rights.description: Grants one party the right to audit the other's records, systems, or compliance.
Audit Rights.plain_language: They may have the right to inspect your books, systems, or operations.
Audit Rights.recommendation: Limit audit frequency (once per year), require advance notice (30 days), and define scope clearly.

Exclusivity.description: Restricts one party from engaging with competitors or alternative vendors.
Exclusivity.plain_language: You may be locked into using only this vendor for this category of service.
Exclusivity.recommendation: Time-limit any exclusivity clause and ensure performance benchmarks are attached.

Minimum Commitment.description: Requires a minimum purchase, usage, or revenue guarantee.
Minimum Commitment.plain_language: You are committed to spending a minimum amount regardless of actual usage.
Minimum Commitment.recommendation: Negotiate usage-based pricing or reduce minimum commitment to a realistic baseline.

Change of Control.description: Defines what happens to the contract if either party is acquired or undergoes a change in ownership.
Change of Control.plain_language: If the vendor is acquired, your contract terms may change or be terminated.
Change of Control.recommendation: Negotiate a right to terminate without penalty if a change of control occurs.

Most Favored Nation.description: Guarantees the signing party receives the best pricing offered to any customer.
Most Favored Nation.plain_language: If they give a better deal to anyone else, you automatically get it too.
Most Favored Nation.recommendation: A favorable clause for buyers — retain it if present.

Anti-Assignment.description: Restricts either party from transferring their rights or obligations under the contract.
Anti-Assignment.plain_language: Neither party can hand this contract off to someone else without permission.
Anti-Assignment.recommendation: Ensure assignment restrictions are mutual and include exceptions for corporate restructuring.

Confidentiality.description: Standard NDA provisions protecting sensitive information exchanged during the engagement.
Confidentiality.plain_language: Both parties agree to keep each other's sensitive information private.
Confidentiality.recommendation: Standard clause — verify it covers your key business information and has reasonable duration.

Limitation of Liability.description: Caps the maximum damages either party can claim.
Limitation of Liability.plain_language: Financial damages are limited to a defined maximum — protects both parties.
Limitation of Liability.recommendation: Ensure the cap is mutual and set at a reasonable level (1–2x annual contract value).

Warranty.description: Defines the duration and scope of product or service warranties.
Warranty.plain_language: The vendor guarantees their product/service will work as described for a set period.
Warranty.recommendation: Standard clause — verify coverage period aligns with your business needs.

Force Majeure.description: Excuses performance obligations in the event of extraordinary circumstances.
Force Majeure.plain_language: Neither party is liable if unforeseen events (natural disasters, pandemics) prevent performance.
Force Majeure.recommendation: Standard clause — ensure the definition of qualifying events is not overly broad.

Dispute Resolution.description: Defines the process for resolving disagreements — arbitration, mediation, or litigation.
Dispute Resolution.plain_language: How disputes are settled if you disagree.
Dispute Resolution.recommendation: For Indian contracts, prefer arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

missing_clause_checklist.reason: Without this, you face unlimited financial exposure. Most critical missing clause.
missing_clause_checklist.indian_context: Indian courts will enforce unlimited liability clauses — no implied cap exists.

missing_clause_checklist.reason: Sensitive business information shared during engagement has no legal protection.
missing_clause_checklist.indian_context: Indian IT Act 2000 does not substitute for contractual confidentiality provisions.

missing_clause_checklist.reason: No obligations on how personal or business data is handled, stored, or deleted.
missing_clause_checklist.indian_context: DPDP Act 2023 creates statutory obligations — contract should align with these.

missing_clause_checklist.reason: Without this, disputes default to court litigation — expensive and slow.
missing_clause_checklist.indian_context: Indian court proceedings average 3–5 years. Arbitration is strongly preferable.

missing_clause_checklist.reason: Either party can exit without notice, causing operational disruption.
missing_clause_checklist.indian_context: 30–90 day notice periods are standard in Indian commercial contracts.

missing_clause_checklist.reason: No guarantee of service quality, uptime, or deliverable standards.
missing_clause_checklist.indian_context: SaaS contracts should specify uptime SLAs and remedies for downtime.

missing_clause_checklist.reason: No protection if extraordinary events prevent contract performance.
missing_clause_checklist.indian_context: Post-COVID, force majeure clauses are considered essential in Indian commercial practice.

missing_clause_checklist.reason: Unclear which jurisdiction's laws apply — creates legal uncertainty.
missing_clause_checklist.indian_context: Without this, courts must determine applicable law — costly and unpredictable.

missing_clause_checklist.reason: No clarity on when, how, or in what currency payments are due.
missing_clause_checklist.indian_context: MSME Act 2006 mandates 45-day payment terms for registered MSMEs — verify compliance.

missing_clause_checklist.reason: Ownership of work product, code, or content created is legally ambiguous.
missing_clause_checklist.indian_context: Indian Copyright Act defaults may not align with commercial intent — explicit clause needed.
